entries.value: CHAPTER 3  WARNING BENEATH THE REEF
MAY 12, 2025  19:30  FIELDWORK BRIEFING
MAY 13, 2025  PUBLIC SHORELINE
CONSENTED INTERVIEW
MAY 16, 2025  SOURCE REVIEW
SIMULATED EVIDENCE MAP
EVIDENCE WALL
MAY 17, 2025  INTERNAL EVIDENCE PACKAGE
CLAIM AUDIT
PUBLIC CASE UPDATE
SEPTEMBER 2026  RETURN TO THE SHORE
SPECIES AND EVIDENCE NOTES
Some voices are difficult for us to hear: beneath seawater, under engine noise, and inside lives that cannot speak to us.
A volunteer sent a maritime notice about underwater blasting planned near Weitou Bay tomorrow. Verify the original page before deciding what fieldwork can establish.
ROLE  You are a volunteer for the fictional Tidewatch Field Station. You may preserve public records, observe from public land and record interviews with consent. You have no enforcement power.
RECORD E01  A public notice can show that work was announced. It cannot prove that work occurred or that dolphins were affected.
Choose a title for the fieldwork assignment.
Blasting will harm Chinese white dolphins
Verify the plan, field conditions and dolphin clues
Will harm turns a risk into a predetermined result. The wording remains in the draft audit trail for later review.
The title defines questions without deciding their answers in advance.
The player saves the full notice, URL, publication time and capture time, then marks a lawful public viewpoint and an exit route. Restricted areas and airspace remain off limits.
At 18:35, construction vessels remain offshore. Engine and metal sounds reach the public shoreline, but the player does not enter the work zone.
Take a wide image containing the sea, distant vessels and fixed landmarks. Record time, weather, direction and the limits of the camera view.
RECORD E02  A distant vessel is visible at 18:38. The image does not show underwater conditions and is not proof that blasting was occurring.
Hello. I am a fieldwork volunteer. May I ask what you have noticed about recent activity at sea? It is fine to say you do not remember.
You can ask, but I do not know much. Judge the information for yourself.
INTERVIEW STATUS  Informed consent given. Record anonymously and do not film the speaker's face.
Did you see or hear anything today that seemed different from usual?
I heard two dull sounds this afternoon. I was on shore and could not see underwater, so I cannot say exactly what they were.
To confirm: you heard the sounds, but did not personally see anything being blasted?
Right. People have mentioned similar sounds since last year, but this was my first time hearing them. I left instead of moving closer.
Did you see any Chinese white dolphins nearby?
A few surfaced not long after the sounds. I have fished here for decades and recognise their pale colour and dorsal fin, but I could not count them or see whether any was injured.
RECORD E03  This is one witness's account. It records personal experience, not confirmed sound source, blast count, species identification, injury or causation.
How should the interview be entered into the evidence log?
Fisher confirms blasting injured dolphins
Record the account; mark source, species and injury unverified
The witness did not see blasting and did not report injury. The sentence changes the testimony and will be rejected during report review.
What the witness heard, saw and could not determine remain separate. The account is useful without pretending it proves more.
Near sunset, several pale backs and dorsal fins appear briefly in the distance. The player stays ashore and records a short telephoto clip.
RECORD E04  The clip may show Chinese white dolphins, pending qualified review. One sighting cannot map their distribution or prove that construction injured them.
Back at the office, news reports, agency statements and public project files enter the source library. Each card must identify who said what and when.
SOURCE E05  A May 16 news report attributed to a provincial fisheries official says two reef-blasting operations occurred on May 13, were stopped that evening, and were reviewed on May 14.
That is a media report of an official's statement. It is not the player's observation, a court finding or a formal notice the player has independently obtained.
SOURCE E06  A May 15 report said no Chinese white dolphin casualties had been reported at that time. No report received does not prove that complete monitoring found no impact.
TIMELINE  The work, reported pause and on-site review all occurred before the player's internal evidence package. The story cannot claim that this player single-handedly caused the pause.
The library opens a species-protection reference and a teaching map beside public project material.
Chinese white dolphins are nationally protected Class I wildlife. Habitat change, human activity and marine blasting are recognised risks worth assessing, not proof of damage in this case.
GAMEPLAY SIMULATION DATA  FOR EVIDENCE-REASONING EDUCATION ONLY  NOT A REAL DISTRIBUTION MAP OR ENVIRONMENTAL-ASSESSMENT CONCLUSION

Some simulated sightings fall outside the simplified survey boundary. The system asks what the real assessment covered, whether reliable source records exist, and whether current evidence can establish a meaningful gap.
Residents not knowing about an assessment does not mean it does not exist. Public availability, technical adequacy and public awareness are three different questions.
SAFE CONCLUSION  This comparison can generate questions for expert review. It cannot declare an assessment invalid or a project unlawful.
The next day, every claim is placed beside its actual source. Each card shows when it was obtained, what kind of source it is and what it cannot establish.
Evidence may remain insufficient. The task is not to force every question into a yes or no answer.
CLAIM 1  Public material supports saying that two reef-blasting operations occurred on May 13 only when the announcement and the media-attributed official statement remain clearly identified.
CLAIM 2  The player must assess whether current records prove that the work injured or killed Chinese white dolphins.
What evidence grade should Claim 2 receive?
Proven: blasting caused dolphin casualties
Insufficient to confirm casualty or causation
There is no casualty record, professional examination or source supporting causation. The overclaim lowers report credibility and triggers revision.
The report preserves the environmental risk while refusing to manufacture an injury or causal finding.
CLAIM 3  A reliable dolphin sighting can justify professional assessment of activity and safeguards. It cannot make every nearby construction project automatically unlawful.
CLAIM 4  An environmental group raised specific concerns about the assessment. That is one party's claim; the simulated map cannot replace regulatory or judicial findings.
CLAIM 5  Delete any statement that the player's May 17 report caused the May 14 pause. The dates disprove that causal story.
The internal report does not auto-generate an accusation. It opens four fixed sections: VERIFIED, SOURCE SAYS, RISK QUESTIONS and STILL UNKNOWN.
VERIFIED  A May 12 public notice announced work for the next day. On May 13, the player documented a distant construction vessel and a clip awaiting species review from a public shoreline.
SOURCE SAYS  An anonymous fisher reported two dull sounds but did not see blasting. A May 16 article attributed two May 13 reef-blasting operations and an evening pause to an agency employee.
RISK QUESTIONS  Chinese white dolphins are Class I protected wildlife. Underwater blasting and habitat change require professional assessment; this report does not claim that an animal was injured.
STILL UNKNOWN  Species, count and condition in the clip; direct source of the sounds; adequacy of assessment and safeguards; later work plans; and independent monitoring results.
AUDIT  The original assignment title predicted harm before fieldwork began. The final report removes that predetermined conclusion.
AUDIT  The draft changed one witness's limited account into proof of blasting and injury. The report restores the original meaning and labels incomplete evidence.
AUDIT  The evidence wall once marked dolphin casualties as proven. With no casualty or causal evidence, that claim is removed rather than quietly hidden.
The source and privacy check passes. The internal evidence package can guide further verification or a report to an authorised body, but it neither proves illegality nor guarantees an outcome.
On July 29, 2025, the player reads a public case statement from Friends of Nature and separates the organisation's allegations from procedural facts.

ORGANISATION'S CLAIM  Friends of Nature alleged new blasting in June and challenged the environmental assessment and safeguards. These are the claimant's positions, not findings already made by a court.
PROCEDURAL FACT  The organisation said a court filing office received its civil public-interest litigation materials on July 28. Receipt is not formal docketing and is not a judgment.
Choose the headline for the July update card.
Court finds the project destroyed dolphin habitat
Group submits case materials; docketing remains unconfirmed
No merits judgment exists at the document-receipt stage. The headline invents a court finding and remains marked for correction.
The headline keeps procedural status separate from the unresolved environmental dispute.

A later August 2026 media report said the court had declined to docket the case in August 2025 on organisational-standing grounds. That procedural result did not decide project legality or ecological harm.
AUDIT  The earlier headline claimed a merits judgment. The later update confirms only a procedural non-docketing report, so the false legal conclusion is withdrawn.
In September 2026, the player returns to the same public shoreline. Port facilities now stand in the distance as a vessel passes offshore.

REALITY UPDATE  One March 2026 agency page called the berths an active marine construction project; a later administrative notice used completed wording for a different purpose. Neither settles the ecological dispute.
The player records a new date, position, weather and visibility. A single return visit remains an observation, not a complete monitoring programme.
The view fades underwater. A pale silhouette passes through blue-green water while stylised echolocation clicks enter the soundtrack for the audience.
This is a symbolic ending, not a real animal record, date or monitoring result. Protecting marine life also means understanding and safeguarding the habitat it depends on.
CHINESE WHITE DOLPHIN  Sousa chinensis  Nationally protected Class I wildlife in China.
METHOD  Record time, place, original source and limitations. Separate direct observation from inference, and never enter dangerous or private areas to obtain evidence.

BOUNDARY  Notices show plans; photographs show what entered the frame; interviews show what a person said. Casualty, ecological effect and legality require evidence and decisions appropriate to each claim.
CHAPTER COMPLETE  TRUTH EMBLEM FRAGMENT ACQUIRED
